newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hong Kong trade eyes Cambodia garment industry.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong trade eyes Cambodia garment industry.

text.p: A high-level Hong Kong trade delegation headed for home on Wednesday upbeat about Cambodia's burgeoning garment sector and said a proposed economic development zone could encourage investment in the country.
The Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) delegates said the Cambodian government offered several carrots to lure factories to their war-scarred country.

These included an ambitious development zone around the southern port of Sihanoukville with modern facilities and easy access to deepwater anchorage, HKTDC Executive Director Michael Sze told Reuters.

"If the zone takes off, we would be quite interested," Sze said, adding that it and two others proposed by Taiwanese investors would go a long way towards addressing concerns about transporting goods on Cambodia's highway system.

A top Industry Ministry official confirmed Cambodia's leaders have approved the 1,000-hectare-plus (2500-acre) zone for foreign investors and said Japanese, Malaysian and South Koreans had expressed interest in constructing the zone.

Common criminals and bands of armed fighters from the Khmer Rouge guerrilla faction, which is fighting a low-intensity war against the Phnom Penh government, on Cambodia's roads can make overland travel difficult and at times, dangerous.
The delegates said they were also worried about Cambodia's high telecommunications costs and unreliable power grid.

The majority of the 18-member HKTDC delegation on the landmark five-day visit were garment makers. But the group also included toy manufacturer Perfekta, INFA Telecom Group and LKK Group, a sauce producer.
Despite the risks, Sze said the companies might be willing to take a chance on Cambodia.
"Nothing ventured, nothing gained," Sze said, pointing out that Hong Kong garment manufacturers have benefitted from taking risks in countries such as Sri Lanka and Burma.
Kenneth Fang, mission leader and chairman of Fang Brothers Knitting Ltd, said the delegation had found Cambodia "better than expected."

Cambodia has pinned high hopes on the garment industry in its effort to lure foreign investors. With 34 factories and as many as 20,000 workers, it is Cambodia's fastest-growing sector. Hong Kong, the world's largest exporter of garments, is a prime target.
